title: Refactoring duplication
learningObjectives: Explain refactoring duplication and implement a maintainable CSS workflow or lab.

understand.concept: CSS refactoring reduces repeated declarations, clarifies component boundaries, and extracts shared tokens or patterns. Refactoring should preserve the rendered behaviour unless a deliberate design change is intended.
understand.whyItMatters: Duplicated styles drift over time and make fixes inconsistent. Refactor incrementally, compare before and after output, and avoid creating abstractions for one-off declarations that do not need reuse.
understand.analogy: Refactoring is reorganising a toolbox so repeated tools have one clear home without changing what the tools do.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the design; implementation must follow browser APIs, CSS behaviour, and accessibility requirements.

explain.narrative: Shared structure is defined once in .card, while the variants express only their differences.
